description.en: WearableQA evaluates AI reasoning over longitudinal wearable sensor data. It comprises 4,084 multiple-choice questions derived from 200 real users' wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographics. Questions are organized into 16 types along data versus health reasoning and single- versus cross-signal axes. Scoring uses multiple-choice accuracy with a known chance baseline.

evidence.snippet: We introduce WearableQA, a benchmark comprising 4,084 10-option multiple-choice questions constructed from the wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographics of 200 real users, each with up to 500 days of daily measurements.

claire_radar.motivation: Recent advances in wearable sensing enable continuous monitoring of physiological and behavioral signals, yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate whether AI systems can reason over a real user's longitudinal wearable record.

claire_radar.paperTitle: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data

source.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data

claire_radar.whyItMatters: Most existing benchmarks do not test reasoning over authentic continuous wearable data, limiting insight into model performance on real-world physiological monitoring. WearableQA provides a diagnostic tool to differentiate model capabilities across distinct reasoning types and signals a largely unsolved challenge, as most models score below 60 percent.
